question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the active GTK-native Linux companion app path, choose a different Linux desktop architecture, or defer Linux companion parity?
rationale: Windows Hub is now documented and released, but Linux remains unimplemented on current main and the active Linux PR is broad, conflicting, and security-sensitive.

options.title: Sponsor GTK-native Linux path
options.body: Use this issue and the active Linux PR to converge on a native GTK/C architecture with scoped security, packaging, and proof requirements.

options.title: Choose another desktop architecture
options.body: Pause the active Linux PR and ask for a narrower Tauri/shared-desktop or other implementation only if maintainers prefer that tradeoff.

options.title: Defer Linux companion app
options.body: Keep Linux to Gateway/CLI support for now and close or park implementation PRs until platform-app work becomes a priority.

recommendation.title: Sponsor GTK-native Linux path
recommendation.body: Use this issue and the active Linux PR to converge on a native GTK/C architecture with scoped security, packaging, and proof requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the tracker and provided the clearest product-direction comments for GTK-native Linux and iterative platform PRs.
